title: Binary Digit Charge
statement: Let $n,p$ be natural numbers and let $v$ be a Boolean list. Suppose either the binary digits of $n$ consist of $p$ ones followed by a zero and then $v$, or they consist of $p$ ones with $v$ empty; and suppose the binary digits of $n+1$ consist of $p$ zeros followed by a one and then $v$. Then the number of ones in the binary digits of $n+1$, plus $p$, equals the number of ones in the binary digits of $n$ plus one, and $p$ is strictly less than the number of binary digits of $n+1$.
